title: Hardening SSH
summary: Host keys, key-based login, sshd_config, and changing it without locking yourself out.

steps.title: SSH proves identity both ways
body: **The server proves itself** with its *host key*. On first connection:
The authenticity of host '10.20.1.10' can't be established.
Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no)?
"yes" stores the key in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. If it ever changes, SSH refuses loudly, because that's what a man-in-the-middle looks like.
The right "yes" compares the fingerprint with one obtained another way (`ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` on the console).
**You prove yourself** with a password (guessable, reusable, phishable) or a **key pair**: the private key never leaves your machine, the public key goes in the server's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

steps.prompt: After a server rebuild, `ssh admin@10.20.1.10` prints `WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!` What's correct?
options: Confirm the new fingerprint out of band (console/admin); only then remove the old line with `ssh-keygen -R 10.20.1.10`
Ignore it; rebuilds always do that
steps.explain: A rebuild explains it, but so would an attacker. Verify, then replace only that entry.

steps.title: Keys only, no root
body: ssh-keygen -t ed25519            # make your key pair (protect it with a passphrase)
ssh-copy-id user@host            # install the public key on the server
PermitRootLogin no           # log in as yourself, then sudo
AllowUsers alice bob         # only these accounts may log in
Validate and reload without dropping sessions: `sshd -t` (silent = OK), `systemctl reload ssh`, `sshd -T` prints the effective settings.
Note: for most keywords **the first value found wins**, so a later duplicate line is silently ignored.
> **Try it for real:** the live lab *Hardening an SSH server* on the Labs page (needs Docker).

steps.prompt: Complete the sshd_config lines: keys only, and no direct root login.
steps.explain: With password login off, guessing attacks can't succeed no matter how many tries.

steps.prompt: Order a safe change to a remote server's SSH config.
lines: Install your public key and test a key login
Open a **new** session to confirm you can still log in
steps.explain: Never close your last working session until a new login works. Installing the key and opening the safety session can happen in either order.
also: Install your public key and test a key login
Open a **new** session to confirm you can still log in

items: Firewall SSH to the admin network only

steps.title: Audit sshd_config
prompt: Write `List<string> Audit(string config)` (lines separated by `\n`). Each line is `Keyword value`; skip blanks and `#` comments; keywords are case-insensitive;
**the first occurrence of a keyword wins**. Return findings in this order:
- `"password login enabled"` unless PasswordAuthentication is `no` (default is yes)
- `"no AllowUsers"` if there's no AllowUsers line
template: Dojo.Eq("defaults", new List<string> { "password login enabled", "no AllowUsers" }, Audit("# empty\n"));

Dojo.Eq("hardened", new List<string>(), Audit("PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
AllowUsers alice bob
"));

Dojo.Eq("first value wins", new List<string> { "password login enabled", "root login allowed" }, Audit("PasswordAuthentication yes
passwordauthentication no
PermitRootLogin yes
AllowUsers alice"));
Dojo.Eq("comments ignored", new List<string> { "no AllowUsers" }, Audit("#AllowUsers alice\n  PasswordAuthentication   no\n"));
hints: Use `TryAdd` so the first occurrence is kept.

steps.title: known_hosts check
prompt: Write `string CheckHost(Dictionary<string, string> knownHosts, string host, string fingerprint)` returning `"new host: verify fingerprint"` if the host isn't known,
`"ok"` if the fingerprint matches, and `"HOST KEY CHANGED: possible man-in-the-middle"` otherwise.
starter: string CheckHost(Dictionary<string, string> knownHosts, string host, string fingerprint)
solution: string CheckHost(Dictionary<string, string> knownHosts, string host, string fingerprint)
if (!knownHosts.TryGetValue(host, out var known)) return "new host: verify fingerprint";
return known == fingerprint ? "ok" : "HOST KEY CHANGED: possible man-in-the-middle";
template: Dojo.Eq("changed", "HOST KEY CHANGED: possible man-in-the-middle", CheckHost(dojoK, "10.20.1.10", "SHA256:Q9zz"));
